subject: VALUE clause
notes: kb/Work PB920 - RE-VERDICTED ON A MEASUREMENT, not on an argument. This row read CONFORMS while the screen had a hole PB555's witnesses could not see, because they all held the literal CLASS fixed: CheckFalseValueDistinct branched on CobolLiteral.IsStringLiteral(literal-2) and `continue`d on a MIXED pair, so `01 X PIC ZZ9.99. 88 X-TEN VALUE " 10.00" WHEN SET TO FALSE IS 10.` compiled clean and `SET X-TEN TO FALSE` left the condition TRUE (MEASURED before the fix: X-STILL-TRUE, XF=[ 10.00], rc 0) - a wrong answer, since SR27 says 'The value of literal-4 shall not be equal to the value of any occurrence of literal-2' and says VALUE, not class and not spelling. On a numeric-edited subject SR6 makes the numeric literal's value the edited image ('literals in formats 1, 2, and 4 of the VALUE clause may be numeric when they shall be converted to their numeric-edited forms according to the rules for the MOVE statement'), and 8.8.4.2.1's NOTE states the consequence the screen must predict ('All comparisons involving numeric-edited data items are alphanumeric or national comparisons, including when the associated VALUE clause is a numeric literal'), with 8.8.4.5.3 GR2 making the condition-name test one of those comparisons. THE FIX IS ONE 'value of' READER: DataBinder.ConditionValueOf answers what a VALUE-clause operand's value IS over its conditional variable - the edited image on a numeric-edited subject, composed by the ONE SR6 composer ValueInitializer.EditedImageOfNumericValue (made phase-neutral, taking (dialectLevel, decimalPointIsComma) rather than an EmitContext, so the binder can ask SR6's question without a second copy of it; ConditionValueRecipeDriftTests now pins THREE named readers and the signature) - and CompareConditionValues orders a pair, answering null when neither a character nor an algebraic pair exists. BOTH ARMS MEASURED at --std 2023 on a freshly built cobol.exe: the cross-class pair and its MIRROR (numeric literal-2, alphanumeric literal-4) are now COBOL2048; the DISTINCT cross-spelling pairs still compile and run (conformance:cases/13.18.63-VALUE/pb920_false_value_cross_class_distinct witnesses numeric-edited both ways round, a numeric subject and an alphanumeric subject), so the screen was not made unconditionally loud. Band 2002+ because the FALSE phrase is a COBOL-2002 introduction; at 85 the two COBOL0900 gates fire alongside the screen.
